LHCb has conducted a study on the decay of $B^0_s$ mesons into two kaons, allowing for an accurate measurement of the x parameter, which characterizes the probability of $B^0_s$ meson mixing and decay over time. By analyzing the transverse momentum distribution of the $B^0_s$ meson and comparing it to theoretical simulations, a more precise value of x was obtained. The measured x value, however, depends on the kinematic range selected for the measurement. By standardizing the selection criteria, an optimized x value was determined and stored for use in future measurements. Additionally, the dependence of certain decay constants and mixing parameters on momentum was investigated, and a new, more precise value of the $B^0_s$ lifetime was derived. This new value, which accounts for previous uncertainties, is in good agreement with earlier measurements but with significantly reduced theoretical uncertainty.

This research paper focuses on the discrete distributed regulation problem, where a stochastic partial differential equation is governed by a randomly fluctuating source term. The study begins with an analysis of the continuous problem and an examination of its parameter convergence properties. The research then moves to the justification of a numerical implementation method and an evaluation of its approximation accuracy. The theoretical findings are supported by empirical evidence obtained from a test case involving the heat equation, in which solution errors are estimated and confirmed through additional calculations. Furthermore, a uniform bound on the test problem is established and demonstrated to hold through an exact solution.

The highest energy particles detected by the Pierre Auger Observatory, for which directional information is available from constituent interactions, were studied to identify large-scale patterns of anisotropy. By plotting energy-dependent arrival directions on a spherical surface and applying Laplace transforms, we discovered significant dipole and quadrupole components at energies above 4 EeV. Notably, the dipole component shows a 9.8 sigma deviation from randomness, orienting towards the constellation of Centaurus, and exhibits southward inclination. Furthermore, quadrupole components display distinct seasonal variations, with the most energetic corpus above 4 EeV revealing complex quadrupolar structures, including variations aligned with the equator and planes of the Milky Way. These findings suggest that medium-energy particles, around 1 EeV, may be influenced by the magnetic field of the Milky Way, while the most energetic particles demonstrate limited galactic correlation and distinct anisotropy patterns unrelated to the plane of the Milky Way.

The ATLAS detector at the LHC gathered p+Pb data with a centre of mass energy of 5.02 TeV and 25 nanobarns of integrated luminosity, enabling a refined analysis of 2-to-4 particle correlations. This study delves into correlated particle structures by examining pairwise and triple/quadruple correlations, classified by their separation in rapidity and azimuthal angle. Notably, charged particle distributions and correlations are found to be independent of nuclear effects, as evidenced by comparison to pp collisions. Moreover, we determined the nuclear modification factor, K, for pairs of particles correlated in $\phi$ within the same $\eta$ range. For mid-central collisions, we discovered a net-charge asymmetry in this correlation and identified a dependence of this asymmetry on the collision centrality.

A general class of noncommutative quantum mechanical systems has been examined within a specific deformable phase space, identified by upper-triangular matrix algebras. By applying a method involving deformed canonical transformations, several known models, including a solvable noncommutative harmonic oscillator and a nonintegrable quantum kink model, were derived. For a particular parameter range, it was found that the original harmonic oscillator retains its integrability, but for other parameter ranges, it becomes nonintegrable. Additionally, some道路 models that are integrable or nonintegrable were found to share the same effective mass formula. In these cases, a connection was observed where the noncommutative deformation and a model-space curvature interact in ways that either preserve or disrupt balance.

An important marker of prognostic value in various cancers is the number of new cancer cells and the classification of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes found within tissue samples. However, assessing these cells requires a highly skilled pathologist to examine the sample under a microscope. Taking advantage of computer vision and machine learning technology, we've developed a federated learning model that teaches a neural network to distinguish between different types of tumor areas and individual cells by training on local patient data. This approach enables multiple medical institutions to collaborate and improve their diagnostic systems, as they can share their knowledge without exchanging sensitive patient information. We tested our approach on microscopic images of colorectal cancer, and results showed our model performed as well as expert pathologists in identifying tumor regions and classifying T-cell types.

In this study, a high-speed optical transmission system is investigated, specifically one that uses a 120-Gbit/s decision feedback equalizer (DFE) to combat chromatic dispersion in an underwater fiber link. Unfortunately, the installation process of underwater communication nodes causes micro-bends in the fiber that generate significant signal disturbances, creating non-Gaussian noise that the equalizer interprets as data changes, thereby feeding forward these errors and reducing system performance. To address this issue, a novel equalization technique is proposed which combines a multi-tap DFE with a adaptive forward filter to recover the affected portions of the signal, thus mitigating the impact of non-Gaussian noise. Our experiments show that while a traditional DFE of five taps is insufficient for effective equalization, the proposed method with its enhanced equalization capability can significantly improve system performance by restoring the degraded eye diagram and increasing the optical signal-to-noise ratio back to its original level.

Deep learning models like Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs) have gained significant popularity in time-series analysis and achieved top rankings in critical benchmarks, including Basic Forecasting, Multi-Forecasting, and Time Series Classification. However, the complicated and massive structure of these networks necessitates a substantial computational memory, hindering their deployment on resource-constrained devices. While network optimization techniques like pruning have been widely used for CNNs, there is limited research on optimizing TCNs, especially considering their unique characteristic of handling both classification and prediction tasks. Our proposed solution, Pruning In Time (PIT), is a novel network optimization framework that accounts for TCNs' duality, enabling the creation of a concise and unified network from the original one. Through the application of PIT, we generated three optimized networks called PIT-0.34, PIT-0.45, and PIT-0.56, which reduce the original network by 34%, 45%, and 56%, respectively, without compromising accuracy. Furthermore, PIT-0.34 and PIT-0.45 demonstrated improved efficiency over the original network in terms of floating-point operations for both classification and prediction, particularly in scenarios with varying input lengths.
It has been proven that every Lie algebra which is a quotient of a free Zinbiel algebra of the same variance is solvable, which means that all such algebras are themselves solvable.

Our analysis aims to enhance the precision of the Pb-Pb interaction angle measurement at the LHC, utilizing a technique that can be applied to all central collisions without the need for additional detectors or calibrations. I employ an adapted method originally proposed by the ALICE collaboration to estimate the average lead-ion pair production angle and its variability across collisions. By analyzing various charged particle fluctuation measures including nucleon scaling, I attempt to isolate the influence of the collision angle. Meanwhile, employing techniques from the ATLAS collaboration to measure the fluctuation in nucleon scaling, I estimate the average lead-ion pair production angle and its variability across collisions. By analyzing charged particle momentum distributions and applying Bayesian methods, I can estimate the average lead-ion pair production angle and its variability as a function of centrality.

This paper stands as the initial exploration of unified inverse representations for a range of extended dual lattice logics (DLEs), specifically focusing on pseudo-complemented, Brouwerian, and Heyting DLEs. By leveraging the adjoint relationship between pullback and left adjoint functors, we have established conditions for various inverse operations, including the pseudocomplement, Brouwer complement, and Heyting complement within a category of extended dual lattices and left adjoint functors. These theoretical advancements are then demonstrated through applications to topological spaces, power sets, and sub-Boolean algeres within Boolean algeres.

Inequalities arising from functional dependencies in tables with empty cells result in contradictions, a phenomenon we explore in this study considering multi-valued attributes within a database context. Building on postulate A (closure property of FDs), which states that an extension of a database relation preserves its functional dependencies, we investigate necessary conditions for adhering to this concept given inequalities caused by missing data. We then relax the closure property to address questions regarding query answering from inconsistent databases and determine the maximum reliable information extractable from such data. We also explore the connection between query answers and reliable information and introduce a method for inferring missing data that maximizes alignment with query results in table extensions that satisfy functional dependencies. We provide a proof of the occurrence of this optimal extension and discuss its relevance to data cleaning tasks.

Building on previous work by Zhang and Wu, this study proposes a novel extension to the Poisson autoregressive model to incorporate time-dependent covariates. A new regression framework, termed time-dependent Poisson autoregression (TPAR), is introduced. Under certain assumptions, a key property known as double asymptotic normality is established for the TPAR model's estimator. The model's estimation process can be broken down into two distinct phases, for which specific convergence rates are established. A simulation study demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method, and a small-scale financial example illustrates its practical application. The paper concludes by suggesting areas for further development, including alternative regression processes and Albrecht-type robustness.

We introduce Neural Descriptor Fields (NDFs), a novel object representation method for 3D objects that are partially or fully visible. NDFs employ an ANE(3)-equivariant network to map 3D descriptor fields, which encode object information from a viewer's perspective. This approach allows for efficient retrieval of objects from various angles and provides a robust basis for downstream tasks, such as object prediction. Pretraining on an object representation task shows that NDFs achieve state-of-the-art results, even with limited training data. Notably, NDFs excel in partial object modeling and outperform existing methods,如玉环表示和其他点云表示方法。

The SiD Detector is one of the two streamlined detectors planned for the future linear linear collider. It features advanced silicon trackers located close to the beam path with exceptional resolution and radiation resistance. It complements the CP-TFC detector, offering a comprehensive detection capability spanning from charged particles to photons, jets, and neutral particles. SiD is being developed under the leadership of US physicists and engineers with participation from 16 universities and national laboratories. This project is undertaking a detailed study to refine its detector design, modifying its geometry and technology to enhance performance and adaptability. SiD's comprehensive simulation system allows for detailed analysis of particle tracking, radiation effects, and data processing, ensuring its robustness and reliability.

We examined the spatial distribution and movement of stars in a globular cluster, specifically Ton2, utilizing a comprehensive dataset of nearly 1000 stars observed with the APOGEE-2 system. We discovered a multi-dimensional structure consisting of a dense central region and two elongated arms stretching out from the nucleus. The movement patterns of the cluster stars revealed a nuclear orbit followed by figure-eight shaped paths, which matched the shape of the cluster. A dynamic model was created to replicate the visual and movement aspects of the cluster. The model recommended a nuclear orbit for the cluster, specifically one with a ratio of 2:1. A simulated profile was created to resemble the observed features of the cluster. The movement residual of this simulated profile was minimal. The dynamic model proposed a mass of 4.09 x 10^4 solar masses and a mass-to-light ratio of 4.38. The detected mass-to-light ratio indicated that the cluster contained a minimal amount of dark matter. A collisional-geometric model with a mass of 4.41 x 10^4 solar masses yielded a mass-to-light ratio of 4.46, indicating that Ton2 was not heavily dominated by dark matter.

The Isabelle Archive of Formal Proofs, a comprehensive collection of community-contributed theories since its start in 2004, has significantly enriched the fields of theorem proving and model checking. It's regarded as both a valuable research resource and a complex collaboration platform. Given its growing intricacy, the need to manage and understand the code has become a major challenge. To address this, the concept of a framework was initially proposed to assist in simplifying and modifying the code. This notion, adapted from software engineering, encompasses a set of principles, structures, and implemented features. However, the framework concept remains theoretical. To advance this idea and promote further development of the Isabelle Archive, we've established a initial definition of framework attributes. This includes establishing design documentation, developing modular components, providing extensibility, maintaining interoperability, and fostering accessibility. Additionally, we've introduced a scoring method to assess and monitor the framework's characteristics quantitatively. This assessment can be performed by humans or Isabelle itself using formalized criteria. As a demonstration of its applicability, we've conducted a detailed analysis and enhancement of the Isabelle/HOL Code Framework, resulting in a more robust and versatile framework. Furthermore, we've released this analysis and associated frameworks as part of the Isabelle/HOL library for community access. This research aims to establish design principles, modular structures, design documentation, and quantitative assessment tools to recognize and enhance the code's features. It also seeks to establish a standard for code generation in Isabelle theories. Additionally

We've determined the precise location of the Yang-Lee edge singularity in zero external magnetic field for classic gases belonging to O(N) universality classes and found it follows a power law in system size with a exponent close to 0.5174, consistent with previous research. This position is specific to the diagonal Drude-Sommerfeld approximation of the susceptibility and has the form of the ratio of gamma functions based on N. This discovery implies that the critical field and the zero-field susceptibility share the same importance near the phase transition, which is also supported by the critical activity theory that involves the scaling of the critical activity with the universal amplitude of the susceptibility.

In statistics and machine learning, particularly within the study of mean field models, it is essential to comprehend how certain quantities change with respect to their inputs. This includes, for instance, understanding the local curvature of the time evolution of the approximate message passing (AMP) algorithm. However, existing second-order AMP algorithms and iterative methods often rely on proving smoothness of various dynamical systems' inputs. We establish a result that ensures the second derivative of a vector function is lower semi-continuous given its first derivative, under weak regularity conditions, and a compact domain. This result enables us to provide a rigorous foundation for a recently observed property of the TAP equation, specifically the local curvature of its free energy, and facilitates the development of correction steps in iterative procedures similar to the AMP. Notably, our proof utilizes tools from non-smooth and semi-smooth analysis, and we believe this result may have broader applications beyond the context of mean field models.

Two approximate methodologies based on patch elements have been computationally examined to determine their limitations and effectiveness in interacting with electromagnetic waves and millimeter-wave signals. Although these methods offer significant efficiency gains over traditional volume-based approaches, they have specific deficiencies when dealing with certain types of surface interactions, particularly curved surfaces, which have been investigated through numerical examples. To circumvent these limitations, at least one alternative has been proposed. Furthermore, the introduction of a novel, highly efficient computational technique for complex three-dimensional surface modeling has been proposed.

The primary objective of this research is to verify the smooth local orbital linearization theorem for smooth hypersingular vector fields on smooth manifolds, where the theorem states that a given fully integrable vector field can be transformed into a set of coordinate linearized vectors through a smooth orbital transformation. This confirms the local orbital linearization theorem as a special case.

This research paper proposes an innovative method to accurately calculate the full electron correlation within molecular systems. It involves utilizing a variational approach with a convolutional variational normalizing flow to represent the molecular wavefunction, allowing for the efficient incorporation of spatial and orbital electron correlation. When combined with the configuration interaction method, this approach is capable of reducing the number of correlated electrons considered while maintaining a high level of accuracy. The proposed method is demonstrated to yield precise results when applied to a variety of molecular systems, including $N$-electron atoms and ion systems.

We analyze an extensive 4.5 square gigarcsecond arc of 3.5 million individual galaxies that were detected using a single deep-field observation from ATLAS3D. This vast arc, first identified in Corson et al. (2021a), is composed of distinct segments spanning across the sky. Notably, it does not correspond to any large-scale structure previously known, such as the Great Wall, and exhibits no correlation with the Cosmic Microwave Background. Furthermore, it is not attributed to foreground effects like radio frequency interference or atmospheric disturbances. Instead, it appears to be of extragalactic origin. Given the arc's large distance, which is estimated at around 10 billion light-years, it significantly challenges current theories in physics. If our measurements are accurate, the arc corresponds to a cross-sectional area that is 10 times larger than its depth. Given current scientific understanding, such an outcome should not be possible.

While photometric aerosol monitoring has been previously used in correlation with ground-based and satellite observations of quality control and mapping, it is now being leveraged in more significant applications due to its potential to track real-time changes in aerosols on the timescale of minutes. This is particularly valuable for modeling and air quality modeling, which are heavily dependent on accurate aerosol input and can benefit from reduced uncertainty through combined modeling and observation. Additionally, with the increased availability of high-resolution cameras and all-sky lenses in the context of novel intelligent monitoring systems, photometric aerosol measurements are being proposed for secondary air quality control and, potentially, primary constraint in atmospheric and climate modeling.

Recently, estimating a object's 6D pose using deep learning has gained significant attention due to advances in deep learning models. While most existing methods focus on predicting pose based on image input from visible dimensions, there is still room for improvement, especially when considering objects with undetermined sides. To address this challenge, this paper presents a new approach called DeepHMap++, a novel method that utilizes a 2D to 2D model learning strategy and a geometric clustering projection model. The unique 2D to 2D learning approach projects possible poses of undetermined sides from visible sides and filters out inaccurate projections using a Deep Sort model. On the other hand, for points that can be directly observed, DeepHMap++ employs a novel method to project 3D space points onto image space. This method creates precise color mappings for potential 6D poses. By combining these two methods, DeepHMap++ is capable of accurately estimating the 6D pose of objects from single image input. The method has been tested and proven effective when integrated with the existing DeepSort method on both linear and circular benchmark datasets of the NPU-RealWorld Pose Estimation dataset.

Peridynamic theories have seen a significant expansion, particularly in recent years, with numerous models addressing different aspects of physics and engineering applications. This bond-based peridynamic framework replaces traditional differential equations with nonlocal integral equations. In this survey, we bridge the gap between peridynamic and other nonlocal mathematical models, highlighting similarities and differences, before delving into bond-based peridynamic dynamics and its connections to rate-independent fracture mechanics. We then examine bond-based peridynamic fluid dynamics, emphasizing the parallels between recent findings and nonlocal variations of the Navier-Stokes equations, before introducing a new dynamic equation and comparing its behavior to existing models.

We introduce GGLasso, a Python library designed to address the Universal Graphical Lasso problem, a crucial step in analyzing high-dimensional systems where edge weights represent significant parameters. If prior knowledge about the positive-definiteness dimension is known, this method allows for more dimension-matching estimates than the standard Graphical Lasso, resulting in more accurate results. Following a key algorithm by Drton and Xue (2016), GGLasso offers performance improvements and easier implementation, providing users with established dimensions or choosing to solve the standard graphically lasso problem.

Designing molecules for drug development necessitates large-scale molecular dynamics simulations to accurately predict and prevent flexible molecular structures from incurring unfavorable conformational effects on target protein binding sites and vice versa. This paper presents a novel stochastic configurational molecular dynamics method that incorporates dissipative forces into the time-reversible molecular dynamics framework, enabling robust and computationally efficient computation of molecular configurations. When applied to testing cases, this method yields molecular configurations that align with benchmark configurational sampling methods and accurately predicts flexible molecular behavior in molecular dynamics simulations of protein-ligand interactions.

Numerical relativity simulations of binary black hole mergers in isolated systems have been extensively studied. However, merging black holes may trigger gravitational instabilities in low-mass particles surrounding them, potentially affecting the outcome of the merger. This outcome depends on how the surrounding particles behave: some may be ejected, while others might collide and generate a dense medium that influences the merger process through forces on the black holes and gravitational effects from the remaining particles. To better understand this, we ran relativistic simulations of binary black hole mergers surrounded by a field of scalar waves, specifically in the mass range where such waves are most prevalent. Our findings showed that for a significant majority of orientations and separations, the binary black hole merger was largely unaffected, with deviations occurring only in scenarios resulting in extreme gravitational waves.

We tackle the long-standing issue of establishing the asymptotic stability of a beam, shaped like an extended 'T', resting on a star-shaped graph, and subjected to a maximal monotone damping system. By leveraging the available compactness properties within a given subspace of $L^2$, we prove that any potential energy dissipation rate equals its supremum, indicating that uniform asymptotic stability is unattainable. However, if specific transversal resonance conditions are met, we demonstrate that exponential asymptotic stability can be achieved. Furthermore, we derive a precise characterization of the rates at which oscillatory modes converge to zero, converging to the uniform asymptotic stability of the system. These convergence rates specifically pertain to non-resonant modes.

Photoacoustic tomography (PAT) combines two imaging techniques to overcome limitations of individual methods. PAT utilizes external excitation sources to generate minimal amounts of radiation while providing high-resolution optical features and electrical safety advantages. To compensate for its relatively low spatial resolution relative to X-ray imaging, PAT techniques can be enhanced by employing specialized materials, such as sonic lenses, to focus the propagation of acoustic waves and improve image resolution through image reconstruction algorithms. Nonetheless, the development of such sonic lens materials has been hinderered by available materials' varying densities and acoustic velocities, often adversely affecting cross-sectional imaging by causing refraction and reflection at material boundaries. In this research, a novel, highly acoustically transparent polymer exhibiting exceptional optical transparency, low hysteresis, and tunable mechanical properties is introduced and demonstrated to be an ideal substitute for expensive alternatives, such as sapphire, by significantly improving the performance of PAT detectors through increased sensitivity, reduced crosstalk, and higher spatial resolution, as evidenced through numerical and experimental results.

The growing complexity of modern technology has led to multi-layered networks that rely on each other for efficient data analysis and a better understanding of their underlying structure. Traditional independent multi-layer analysis methods are no longer sufficient, necessitating a new approach that takes into account the interdependent nature of these nodes across the different layers. A new metric, the Reliant Node Eigenvector (RNE) centrality, has been developed to evaluate the significance of nodes within dependent multi-layer networks by calculating the sum of weights from adjacent nodes in each layer and calculating the eigenvalues of these weighted connections. A test case was conducted on a multi-layered network representing the interconnections between the U.S. Senate, House, and presidential veto powers to demonstrate the effectiveness of the RNE centrality in identifying the most influential nodes within this type of dependent network.

We tackle the issue of correcting raw images that are affected by motion blur, color mismatch, and noise. These problems are interconnected, which suggests a raw-to-raw transformation, accomplished through a newly devised network called D^3, developed end-to-end. However, a lack of available training data for motion blur in raw images restricts model generalisation. Therefore, we created a set of synthetic training images with controlled levels of motion blur, demosaicking patterns, and noise, supplemented by a demosaicking simulation module. This allows for the generation of distorted raw images suitable for model training. Having designed an appropriate loss function that catagorises the various operations, which leads to two distinct approaches: joint learning or sequential learning. Ultimately, the proposed joint learning method surpasses several benchmarks, demonstrating significant improvements in PSNR and SSIM scores over existing methods.

Recently, we demonstrated that key principles of relativity are compatible with Dirac's equation, by deriving a form of the equation specific to R-Minkowski space-time and associated momentum space. This new equation was then shown to have a profound mathematical property, where the commutator of two Hamiltonians yields the negative of the total energy operator, satisfying a remarkable identity known as HF = -[H,p]. As a consequence, multiple solutions to the equation can be derived from its planar eigenstates, characterized by a discrete, doubly infinite set of quantum numbers. Furthermore, in the limit where quantum effects become negligible, these solutions converge to those of the standard Dirac equation in conventional Minkowski space-time.

This paper introduces a comprehensive set of techniques for making observations,
making inferences, and learning from data to uncover causal connections.
Additionally, a Python framework is presented to facilitate exploration
by integrating relevant libraries such as do-calculus, structural equation
models, and neural networks with interventional and observational data.
Using this framework, we demonstrate how to answer interventional queries,
perform sensitivity analysis, and fit interventional and causal models to
data, followed by an assessment of model performance and interpretability.

Water seal velocity ranges for water-borne robots have been widened through the development of hydro jets that reduce water splashing during surface landings. However, optimizing jet system design to minimize both seal forces and system complexity remains challenging. This study investigates the impact of water ejection patterns on surface seal forces during a sphere's water landing, specifically when moving at intermediate speeds without jets, and compares it to two jet configurations: uniform and concentrated streams. Experimental results show that surface seal forces normalized by pressure and area exhibit distinct behaviors, and the influence of jet design is significantly observed in the intermediate speed range, where seal performance is poorly understood.

We investigate the implications of global symmetries in Type IIB supergravity, a theory that serves as an approximation to Type IIB string theory and influences the four-dimensional effective field theory derived from it. By focusing on consistent Kähler transformations and deriving the most general set of couplings that respect a U(1) R symmetry in a canonical supergravity theory, including a generalized Weyl-rescaled theta-term, we establish the associated current and anomaly. This analysis enables us to identify and eliminate spurious global symmetries in a four-dimensional N=2 supergravity theory obtained from type IIB string compactifications. By parameterizing the two-loop Type IIB scalar potential and determining the transformation properties of its components, including vacuum expectation values for moduli and dilaton and the generalized Weyl-rescaled theta-term, we discover that VV-modes and a specific non-holomorphic two-loop factor provide a mechanism for R-symmetry breaking that is independent of non-perturbative effects. This mechanism is further supported when adding an O4-planes to the compactification, which allows for a threshold shift of the moduli-monodromy invariant theta-term that could potentially break U(1) R-symmetry and generate a small supergravity scale.

We tackle the security concerns arising from imperfections in security hardware, which can give rise to side-channels and crashes, that adversaries can exploit to learn about other software's data without direct access. We present an alternative approach, called Suhw, which utilizes physically-isolated hardware for running solely by one application, thereby minimizing trust in the hardware's inherent security. We demonstrate that modern computers, which typically include CPU-enforced isolation, can be repurposed for Suhw, allowing for efficient execution of multiple Suhw applications on the same machine with minimal performance loss, which averages around 1.37 times for workloads that include encryption, decryption, sandboxed JavaScript, and database management.

We examine the impact of substantial corruption in data within the context of policy gradient methods used in reinforcement learning. Specifically, we investigate how the magnitude of corruption influences the stability of policy gradient methods. Our research reveals that conventional PG algorithms are vulnerable to large-scale corruption, causing them to converge to incorrect solutions. In contrast, we develop two robust variations of the policy gradient method - Resilient Policy Gradient (RPG) and Resilient Policy Gradient with Variance Reduction (RRVR) that are capable of functioning effectively even in the presence of significant corruption. Our proposed methods achieve a compromise between accuracy and stability by integrating an empirical covariance matrix to mitigate the impact of corrupted information. Theoretical and practical evaluations of our algorithms demonstrate their capability to produce reliable and consistent results despite the presence of data corruption.

We investigate an infinite box game on the real number line and demonstrate that, under the assumption of choice, there exists a winning strategy for the player selecting the box at a rational time. This implication arises from the fact that it would be possible to create a winning sequence for players picking an odd number of items, which contradicts known results under the assumption of choice in situations involving an advantage of two. However, this latter claim has already been addressed by Ketonen and Solovay (1977). Moreover, we provide a choice-less solution under the assumption of choice that involves a connection to a measure of compact support spanning the whole real number line. Given that such a measure inherently possesses this property under choice but its non-chosen equivalent has previously been disproven by Miller (1987).

Cubanite ($CuFe_2S_3$) displays semimetallic properties with strong superconductivity in its parent state, exhibiting strong correlations and long-range order, which include magnetic and charge order. Through detailed analyses using X-ray spectroscopy, theoretical calculations, and experimental magnetic data, we discovered that cubanite exhibits orbital selectivity. Notably, we found that the $t_{2g}$ $3d$ orbitals of iron behave in a strongly correlated manner, whereas the sulfur $3p$ orbitals remain broad and weakly interacting. This coexistence of strongly and weakly interacting systems allows us to model cubanite using a four-band model. Comparing it to kagome-based compounds, we find that cubanite exhibits a distinct magnetic pattern, resulting from its unique crystal structure and strong coupling between orbitals.

A new effect called giant Rabi fluctuation is discovered that is ten times stronger than previously known examples, occurring in material quantum emitters that do not require an external magnetic field. These anomalies are caused by material-specific fluctuations in an external environment and can be utilized to generate high-fluctuation Rabi oscillations, enabling faster and more accurate calibration of emitters through a new, joint measurement of fluctuating Rabi frequencies between two emitters.

We examined a two-dimensional non-symmorphic wall-paper lattice and found two types of wall-network structures with different geometries.
By using a tight-binding model, we discovered that Dirac points can appear within these 2D networks without requiring symmetry-protected linear crossings, with their positions controllable through various parameters.
Specifically, tuning the unit-cell size and lattice connectivity can alter the size of the mini-bands and thus the location of the Dirac points, while also offering simultaneous non-interfering multi-orbula and multi-bands within a single model.
Furthermore, we observed that both valley and spin Hall effects are strongly induced near the Dirac points by the opening of a non-zero gap, resulting in a topological insulator state.
These effects yield large values for the valley and spin Hall coefficients by manipulating the unit-cell and connectivity, and similar properties are induced by the non-zero Chern numbers in both cases.
Also, we found that both valley and spin Hall hall coefficients are closely correlated with the valley and spin separations, while both of these quantities are significantly altered by the unit-cell and connectivity, as well as by the onsite energies and connectivity between adjacent electrons.
Thus, our theory indicates that our theoretical calculations indicate that both valley and spin separation can be efficiently manipulated by both geometric design and electronic connectivity within a single and highly tunable 2D non-symmorphic wall-network lattice.

Quantum states that exhibit phase coherence are commonly used in applications like interferometry and are also entangled users can employ a shared single-photon to create a phase-coherent GHZ state, also known as quantum catalysis. This phenomenon enhances their collective capabilities without ever becoming entangled themselves. Although previously only theoretical, non-classical catalysis has now been observed in a practical setting using semi-catalytic quantum catalysis. A single-photon is used to facilitate a common beam-splitter through which two users send their laser beams, resulting in a single-photon catalyzed Bell state. The level of coherence in this outcome can be controlled by adjusting the amount of entanglement between the users.

We provide a detailed explanation of bivectors within the Newman-Penrose formalism for General Relativity, using a 2+2 coordinate system that splits spacetime into pairs of complex surfaces. This approach builds on previous work by M.T. Jennings that seeks to make advanced GR techniques more accessible through algebraic geometry. By examining NP components of the Maxwell equations for an electromagnetic field, we discovered a direct relationship between the coefficients representing the electric and magnetic fields and a geometric property known as the Atiyah class of a certain complex surface. This relationship reveals a deeper connection to the Weyl curvature tensor in GR.

Designing new polymers is crucial for creating advanced materials because of their ability to control a polymer's behavior during manufacturing and application. A widely used method for polymer design involves combining monomers with varying molecular building blocks. However, finding a set of monomers that align with the desired integer control parameters is a complex task due to the multiple constraints that monomers are subject to. This study introduces a method to derive new monomers from basic molecular molecular building blocks by utilizing an efficient linear regression to identify building blocks specific to a molecular method. This method was successfully applied to modify a superabsorbent adsorbent polymer by inferring new monomers suitable for the application. Copyright 2018 authors.

This paper provides an in-depth explanation of direct transcription methods, including direct collocation and implicit collocation, for solving optimal control problems. We discuss their benefits in preserving control system dynamics when adding a performance optimization objective, especially in nonlinear systems. We then explore direct transcription approaches, noting their connection to modern numerical methods like collocation and spectral methods. We also cover their implementation using Generalized B-Splines (GBS) and their suitability for real-time applications. Direct transcription's ability to represent infinite-dimensional solution spaces makes it a previously overlooked alternative to traditional numerical methods. We then walk through a case study on dual-patient mechanical ventilation during the COVID-19 pandemic, where an air compressor delivers customized pressure waves to two patients through parallel circuits. Our computed pressure profiles match recently reported experimental results, and our approach offers a path for optimizing air compressor design for effective dual-patient ventilation.

Identifying tumors in the esophagus from CT images is a significant issue in medical image analysis due to its difficulty. Accurately pinpointing and measuring the location of tumors in CT images obtained from a patient's scan is crucial for diagnosis, treatment planning, and monitoring of the disease. Evaluation reports indicate that radiologists assess the severity of the illness by visually analyzing CT images. For enhanced diagnostic, therapeutic, and monitoring outcomes, reducing the evaluation burden is essential. Since evaluting multiple features in CT images is complicated due to variations in density across slices, a new model called Data Adaptive Unet (DDAUnet) has been proposed to address this issue. By incorporating skip connections that adapt to focal areas and an attention mechanism, DDAUnet pays closer attention to key regions. From these features, an optimized search strategy is used to determine the ideal unit structure and parameter settings. Experiments show that BBIG-04, a model found to be among the best performing in a recent competition, can be rivaled by DDAUnet even with a smaller number of parameters. Furthermore, F1, IoU, and Dice metrics used in medical image segmentation indicate that the proposed method yields highly competitive results with improved performance over BBIG-04.

Well log analysis in reservoir characterization and geosteering is heavily
influenced by the interpretation of logs by engineers. Traditional methods often
rely on expert-based approaches to interpret wells, which can be time-consuming
and costly, especially when applied to real-time geosteering scenarios with
multiple wells. Moreover, a significant drawback of this approach is its
inability to effectively communicate uncertainties in log interpretations to
drillers, ultimately affecting decision-making processes. A novel, objective
method is necessary to resolve these challenges. This paper introduces an
innovative framework that utilizes ensemble-based techniques to analyze well
logs and account for various sources of uncertainty, including log tool
variations, environmental effects, and reservoir properties. Moreover, this
methodology is applied to real-time geosteering to optimize decision-making by
taking into consideration the uncertainties in well log interpretations.

Named entity recognition (NER) is a fundamental task in natural language processing and serves as a starting point for various other NLP applications. NER plays a crucial role in extracting relevant information from text, including understanding the overall structure of documents. Despite its significance, traditional NER methods often struggle to accurately identify complex entities that rely on nested structures, which is often overlooked in existing evaluations. In this study, we introduce a comprehensive framework for nested NER that accounts for the structural dependencies often found in text, expanding the scope of entity parsing to include nested structures. To achieve this, we propose using a nested graph representation to capture the full parsing structure and a decoding-based approach based on a search algorithm to efficiently parse complex entities. Our experimental results on three distinct datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, outperforming current state-of-the-art models in F1 scores on both binary and multi-class NER classification tasks. Overall, our work highlights the importance of considering text structure in NER and showcases how a complementary perspective can enhance the performance of existing models.

We will explain the connection between finding bitangent lines to plane quartics and a specific type of tropical object called a degree four binode. This link originates from recent discoveries by Cavalieri, Clader, and Payne. Using this connection, we can expand on existing work to show that if the tropical binode has certain properties (being resolvable and having real branches), then we can derive formulas for related geometric entities over p-adic numbers and real numbers. These formulas are derived from specific counting functions. This approach yields the first instances of bitangents lines to irreducible plane quartics that are defined by rational numbers.

This research focuses on position estimation in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) using Triangulation, Trilateration, and Tri-lateralation methods, and evaluates three approaches for determining the positions of target nodes. We developed three algorithms: Traditional Technique (TT), Traditional Technique in presence of Cross-Technology Interference (TTI), and Reversed Traditional Technique (RTT). TT and RTT calculate distance based on Traditional Technique, while TTI uses a conventional WSN technique (e.g., TOA, TDOA, RSSI, RSS). We integrated these methods into a single hybrid technique to enhance the accuracy of target node localization, and implemented a simulation using CrossNet and C++ to evaluate the results, yielding 99.999999999999999824% accuracy.

This paper provides an in-depth examination of code-mixed NLP, noting the current limitations and issues that arise in this field, particularly in relation to multilingual societies. Our research explores the intricacies of NLP for low-resource, script-diverse languages that code-mix, such as Hindi-English. By code-mixing two languages with different writing systems, languages like Hindi present unique NLP challenges. Our study also considers potential factors influencing social media users to switch languages and mix codes, which could facilitate the development of code-mixed NLP models. Ultimately, we believe a well-defined semantic sequence in a preferred code is the key to achieving accurate NLP for code-mixed data, which could pave the way for effective model development in this area.

Assessing the performance of automated description systems for images is a complex task. While there are established methods, they often fall short due to inconsistencies in human writing styles, grammatical variations, and subjective interpretations. These factors make human-generated descriptions an imperfect reference point for evaluating system output. To address this limitation, we propose generating diverse sets of diverse sets of diverse descriptions for a set of images, which may not accurately reflect the true performance of automated systems.

We propose a novel methodology for generating diverse sets of descriptions for images, which we employ to evaluate commonly used evaluation datasets. Our results indicate that commonly used datasets significantly differ from sets of diverse descriptions generated by humans, leading to misleading performance metrics. We provide a mathematical framework for quantifying diversity, which we utilize to demonstrate that human-generated benchmark data does not adequately reflect the true ground ground truth.

In fact, in many cases, this leads to substantial discrepancies between system-perceived and actual image description capabilities. We provide a novel approach for effectively evaluating automated image description systems by combining our diverse human-generated datasets with machine learning algorithms. Our results indicate that this method yields ranking and relevance metrics that closely resemble those of human assessments, exceeding the efficacy of commonly used evaluation datasets.

Tantalum oxide materials, with diverse crystallographic forms, are key in numerous applications including capacitors, catalysis and piezoelectric devices.  However, the complex simplicity of intermediate Ta$_2$O$_5$ phases makes it challenging to control their properties due to multiple coexisting crystallographic structures.  Our study utilizes first-principles calculations to accurately identify a low-energy Ta$_2$O$_5$ phase, initially solving its atomic arrangement through a Monte Carlo method.  Next, we verified that it is a stable, isolated system with minimal energy by applying the density functional theory.  Distinguishing characteristics of this phase include isolated T$_d$ tantalum atoms, an extensive insulating gap and exceptional mechanical stability.  Interestingly, its electronic gap is exceptionally large at around 3.54 eV.  Our analysis also identified two additional polymorphs with even higher energy barriers and substantial stability.  Ta$_2$O$_5$-MC exhibits extraordinary mechanical properties with a tensile stiffness of 212 GPa and an elastic compliance of 4.7 GPa, along with a highly transparent visible range.  Its crystallographic stability is confirmed by simulations of uniaxial compression and tension, as well as a phase transition to the body-centered cubic structure at 315 GPa.  Ta$_2$O$_5$-MC exhibits complete mechanical stability and 100% phase recovery after

Previous studies attributed a significant portion of the spread of misinformation in online communities to influential individuals who shared false information with their extensive networks. Our research uncovered an underappreciated phenomenon known as the Big Geographic Shift (BGS) that accounted for over half of the circulation of geographical-related misinformation in certain sub-Reddit groups. We defined BGS as occurring when users shared posts originating from distant geographic locations with their nationwide Reddit peers. Notably, analyses revealed that accounts responsible for Ags experienced significant increases in account age, follower counts, and activity levels prior to posting false information, suggesting that while well-known influencers do spread misinformation, a less significant group of active participants also contributes to the circulation of such information in certain online communities.

Recent breakthroughs in the spread of fast information have sparked a growing interest in developing intelligent systems capable of pinpointing malicious campaigns that spread information at unprecedented speeds. However, identifying suspicious incidents in high-speed information flows proves challenging due to a lack of identifiable boundary for anomalous content and a vast number of legitimate users that share and spread content rapidly. To tackle this problem, we propose a novel approach called Suspicious Incidents Detection (SID) that leverages a unique property of suspicious flows where a significant portion of users engage with and share a large portion of sources in an unusually concentrated manner. By applying a graph-based algorithm to monitor user sharing behavior, our approach aims to detect highly active and interconnected users that facilitate the widespread propagation of suspicious content. We implemented and evaluated our SID on large-scale Twitter datasets and were surprised to find that we achieve accurate results even in high-speed flows of more than 50 million users. Our study demonstrates that our approach can also effectively detect suspicious incidents in moderate-speed flows, as shown with real-world datasets containing fast-spreading COVID-10 rumors, where our model outperformed baseline models and manually labeled baselines.

Humans teach robots effective movements through demonstration, which can be tracked using sensors like cameras and accelerometers.  Studies show that certain techniques when performing tasks are consistently used across different humans, leading to optimal or near-optimal results.  However, finding these patterns through data alone proves difficult.  As a solution, analyzing human teachers' movements through symbolic methods may reveal efficient strategies for executing tasks.  This study suggests using plan graphs to identify patterns in kinematic data, creating compact data representations that can be used to generalize robot learning from human demonstrations.

Building on previous research, we propose an algorithm to randomly generate ordered trees according to a specified probability, capable of handling trees with nodes categorized into distinct groups. This algorithm is a modified version of the Bartosek method. We prove that when applied, it yields the desired distribution for an important subset of intractable cases. Additionally, we demonstrate that it can be used to efficiently generate the lexicographically first tree satisfying a given property according to a defined criterion, and this approach can also be applied to generate sampling sets for numerical integration.

The equations of motion for a particular sigma model on an SU(2)/U(1) manifold, associated with a specific background charge, can be transformed via a particular substitution into the fourth-order Painlevé-IV equation. This connection enables a deeper analysis of the conformal field theory through an examination of the holomorphic properties of its correlation functions, which in turn yields valuable insights into the asymptotic behavior of solutions to non-linear differential equations. A key finding is the identification of Stokes lines within a complex p-plane, which dictate the interplay between power law and exponential components in the asymptotic behavior of solutions to the fourth-order Painlevé-IV equation.

We devise a method to identify any unseen gravitational source influencing the orbits of recently discovered planets and present an estimate of its maximum mass. By applying this method, no hidden massive celestial bodies were found within the sensitive range of the Sun in the planetary system. However, subtle discrepancies between observed and predicted positions of the inner planets leave some room for improvement, possibly due to unaccounted-updated ephemerides of the Sun, Earth, and Mars. A hypothetical unseen celestial body in a circular, mid-sized orbit would need to be at least 10 to 20 times more massive than the Earth to be detected, or at least 1 to 2 times as massive in a highly elliptical orbit with a semi-major axis under 100 astronomical units. In contrast, the anomalies affecting the outer planets are much more pronounced, suggesting any undetected object in a circular orbit closer than Neptune is at least 45 times as massive than the Earth, while anything between Neptune and Pluto requires at least 3 to 10 Earth masses. Notably, Planet Nine hypotheses propose various undetected objects in high semi-major auctions exceeding the sensitive range for 1 to 10 Earth mass asteroids, with some exceeding the detection limit for super-Earths or even Neptune-mass planets in more compact orbits.

To enhance translation accuracy, especially for low-resource languages, our approach leverages a monolingual lexicon. By fine-tuning an existing Neural Machine Translation model with a source language lexicon, encoded as a lean memory bank, we observe notable improvements. This is depicted through a simple architectural diagram. Empirical results confirm our hypothesis: translating to a high-resource language yields significant gains, while in low-resource scenarios, a single model can achieve results comparable to a model without a memory component. Notably, the model with the lexicon memory also outperforms a model trained from scratch using a bilingual corpus.

Researchers have suggested that specific patterns in the Cosmic Microwave Background, such as low multipoles and an equatorial great circle, could be evidence of a previous universe from the Conformal Cyclic Cosmology model. A statistical analysis was conducted to examine the significance of these patterns in relation to standard inflationary theory. Furthermore, the inherent symmetry of the $\Lambda$CDM model was used to assess the expected frequency of these structures under both the RCC and $\Lambda$CDM models. A statistical analysis combining the likelihood of these features under both models indicates that the low multipoles and great circle are unlikely when viewed through the lens of the standard $\Lambda$CDM model. Although they appear statistically significant, the characteristics of an additional dipole and a latitude bias suggest that the low multipoles and great circle might be artifacts resulting from our position in the sky and the movement of the solar system. Moreover, a potential violation of the statistical independence assumption in the analysis is identified, which is expected to lower the calculated significance.

This paper builds upon the development of a Yamabe flow by Zhang, providing proof that the flow converges to the minimal scalar curvature when starting from specific initial data. Additionally, we demonstrate the existence of solutions for a time period when given suitable initial conditions.

To rapidly adapt to new tasks involving a limited number of labeled samples, few-shot learning aims to generalize effectively from limited data. Despite significant progress, existing methods often struggle with regular, fully-labeled datasets due to their over-fitting tendency to mean-encoded data. This document outlines a potential pathway to enhance the ability to learn from limited datasets by encouraging the use of representative prototypes, which can be derived from rich, diverse datasets using transfer learning. We demonstrate this approach's validity through improved performance on the Stanford Dogs dataset and balanced results between limited and fully-labeled tasks on the CIFAR-20 dataset.

Multiple sparse data domains often exist within the same recommendation system, but underutilized, they can offer complementary information that's crucial for enhancing preference knowledge and supporting cooperative recommendation. However, existing data domain-specific models fail to capture this complementary utility, while cross-domain approaches, although transfering knowledge, neglect specific domain preference knowledge. To address these challenges, we introduce a novel, innovative Multi-Sparse-Domain Cooperative Recommendation (MSDCR) model that's based on Enhanced Comprehensive Aspect Preference Learning (ECAP). A novel dual-function Comprehensive Aspect is designed to both transfer and preserve domain-specific preference information, while a Multi-head Attention Network is introduced to weight the importance of different preference information. To optimize the complex objective function, a simple yet effective Multi-Sparse-Domain Cooperative Optimizer (MSCO) leverages both evolutionary computation and gradient-based methods. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed model significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.

To enhance optimization problem solvers, particularly those involving convex sets defined by cones, we integrate cone solvers into a nonlinear programming (NLP) framework. By representing an NLP's objective and constraints in a conic format, converting its first-order optimality conditions into a second-order cone program (SOCP) yields a highly efficient system of equations. This innovation allows for the creation of a novel hybrid solver, Hypatia, that combines a Newton-based NLP algorithm with a specialized SOCP solver, leveraging the efficiency of the latter in efficiently updating the cone components. The efficacy of Hypatia is demonstrated through multiple test problems, outperforming existing nonlinear interior point methods.

Multi-factorial environments pose significant challenges for machine learning classification, particularly when dealing with medical imaging data affected by multiple suboptimal factors beyond simple graphical transformations. Existing methods for MRI quality assessment have struggled to generalize well to new centers and imaging parameters due to excessive overfitting. This research seeks to enhance the implicit complexity control of deep convolutional neural networks to prevent excessive overfitting and enable effective generalization to novel, multi-factorial data sets. Rather than relying on explicit complexity regulation, this study explores the implicit regulatory capabilities of fully connected layers and employs a strategically minimized number to enhance model performance. Furthermore, it proposes data augmentation techniques using generative models to further boost classification accuracy, addressing both real and synthetic data augmentation challenges. Experimental evaluations across two distinct brain MRI data sets highlight the efficacy of proposed implicit complexity control and enhanced data augmentation strategies, demonstrating significant performance improvements. This research is expected to establish a robust foundation for high-quality medical image analysis through implicit complexity control in deep learning networks.

To examine how private electric vehicles influence the recovery of power networks following disruptions, this research utilizes a methodology that incorporates decentralized optimization and multi-agent technology. We explore the potential of private EVs to power critical infrastructure during outages and develop a framework where EV owners can sell electricity to essential services and buy it back at lower prices to recharge their vehicles. Furthermore, we propose using evolutionary algorithms to find optimal recharge and selling strategies for EVs, along with an effective way to coordinate between private EV owners and power network operators for a more resilient power system. We validate this approach through numerical tests based on real power network and outage data, along with publicly available bus scheduling information.

Recently, Intel introduced Optane DC Persistent Memory, an innovative type of main memory that retains data even after power loss, enabling operating systems and applications to resume from the last state upon system reboot without extensive restoration. This report examines the performance capabilities of Optane DC PM with an operating system support, specifically DAX (Direct Access) which permits direct CPU-to-memory data transfer. However, due to Optane DC PM's limited addressing capacity, the DAX driver necessitates workararound to utilize the full 48-bit physical address space available in modern x86 processors. An analysis of data access speeds for both single and bulk operations with Optane DC PM reveals significant variations in throughput when compared to DRAM, particularly as operational scales increase.

Multi-agent path finding is a well-established issue in the agentic systems realm and deals with determining individual paths for multiple agents to move from starting positions to target positions within a grid, abiding by various constraints to avoid collisions and ensure efficiency. A specific variant of this problem, known as the last-agent meeting problem, focuses on finding paths that lead all agents to a single meeting point. While various solutions exist, the concept of a meeting point can feel unnatural to the agents involved, prompting us to introduce a novel approach called Multi-Agent Recurrent Meeting, also known as MARC. This solution is inspired by the idea of intrinsic motivation and involves agents being driven to meeting points, referred to as "seeds," which they can generate. By alternating between moving to seeds and generating new ones, our last-agent meeting algorithm successfully finds an optimal meeting point for all agents to reach. Moreover, by incorporating a seed-generation mechanism, agents can cooperate to achieve a meeting on a deadline in more instances than would occur by chance. Our method achieves a 99% success rate on meeting a deadline in 100-agent trials within an 800-step timeframe, and we believe this solution has the potential to be applied to other variant path-finding issues as well.

This paper examines the structural, electronic, and magnetic characteristics of GdSn3, CmSn3, and the series GdxCm1-xSn3 (x = 0.25, 0.50, 0.75) using a combination of relativistic and non-relativistic full-potential linearized augmented plane wave and local orbital calculations within the density functional theory framework. Both R-3m and P-3m1 space groups were used to investigate these compounds. Our findings suggest that both space groups are stable for both GdSn3 and CmSn3, with additional verification provided through molecular dynamic calculations showing GdSn3 in the R-3m space group and CmSn3 in both P-3m1 and R-3m space groups. We predict the lattice constants and bulk modulus of both GdSn3 and CmSn3 to be in line with available experimental and theoretical data. Both compounds are predicted to be mechanically stable, with both P-3m1 and R-3m space groups showing both compounds to be stable. We further predict both GdSn3 and CmSn3 to be half-metallic in nature with both P-3m1 and R-3m space groups, with both compounds displaying both up and down spin channels to have band gap characteristics. We also investigate the magnetic moments of both Gd and Cm in GdSn3 and CmSn3, with GdSn1

An innovative method for forecasting the number of particles (specifically baryons and light mesons) that occur in high-energy collisions of protons has been methodologically outlined and tested. This method, based on a revised version of the MCMC approach, utilizes an existing model to account for the particles and utilizes the CMSSW framework to process the data. It was initially utilized at a meeting of the BABar collaboration in 2011, and subsequently demonstrated with more computational power, was found to produce accurate results, though with slower results than a like-method but different approach. When applied to collisions of proton-antiproton at a energy level of 1.96 TeV, and using data from the Do collaboration, it was able to accurately capture the number of baryons produced in collisions.

We provide a novel, simplified, and streamlined proof of the previously established foundation theorem for irreducible Coxeter groups of B-type, achieved through an innovative, modular argument. This newly discovered proof enables an equally straightforward and fundamental basis for classifying infinite B-type Coxeter groups, which can be derived from the fundamental theorem of finite B-type Coxeter groups.

Utilizing an ensemble approach for analyzing cosmological parameters, researchers discovered that the impact of a galaxy's foreground on the apparent brightness of Type Ia supernovae, or weak lensing, significantly affects our understanding of dark energy. To accurately estimate the distances of these supernovae and counter the influence of weak lensing, researchers must obtain a precise measurement of the foreground galaxy counts. A analysis of the Pantheon dataset, consisting of 1027 Type Ia supernovae, illustrated this phenomenon by calculating the apparent magnitudes and number counts of the galaxies in front of them. r-spectra were utilized to isolate the lensing impact in each supernova system, resulting in a statistical shift of 0.07 milliamperes and a corresponding increase of 8.4 percent in the apparent brightness. R, on the other hand, experienced an decrease of 0.03 milliamperes and a corresponding 3.6 percent increase in apparent brightness. These findings have a notable impact on the inferred values of dark energy's density and equation of state, leading to an overestimation of 0.03 and 0.02, respectively. This study underscores the significance of accounting for weak lensing in our investigation of dark energy's properties.
These are the introduction remarks for a research session on Nonlinear Stochastic PDEs, specifically focusing on "Equations of Heat Type".

This letter introduces a novel structure called T-joint made from silicon-on-insulator material, which has an unusual property of allowing light to split and recombine without losing intensity. By utilizing two T-joints in a twisted configuration, we can create light sources that split equally into two paths for any given input. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that these structures can be integrated with existing technologies to create on-chotronic devices by combining optical and electrical signals.

MRI technology utilizes radio waves to scan the human body and obtain precise, pain-free diagnostic images. By analyzing these images, medical professionals can assess injuries and illnesses within the body. Advanced medical imaging, supported by computer-aided diagnosis systems, enables expert examination of features within MRI images, enabling the detection of brain tumors. This project involved creating a sophisticated algorithm to identify and classify tumors in MRI images, resulting in a system capable of detecting tumors and distinguishing between benign and malignant types.

The n-th Bernoulli number, denoted by $B_n$, can be effectively represented through the determinant of a specific symmetric matrix with entries $a_{ij} = \frac{1}{i+j-1}$ for $i,j\geq 1$. We demonstrate that multiplying this determinant by $(2n-1)!!$ yields a rational number $r_n$. By expanding the determinant of a modified matrix with an additional parameter, we establish the relationship $r_n = \frac{B_{2n}}{(2n-1)!!^2}$, which directly links the determinant to the Bernoulli numbers.

The difficulty in distinguishing between the effects of stellar activity and those of exoplanets has motivated researchers to investigate how to mitigate the former's influence on radial velocity measurements. A method to reduce stellar activity noise is least-squares deconvolution, but its effectiveness relies heavily on choosing an appropriate line sample. This line selection process was examined for LSD in a study focusing on two line selections: a set of lines with specific parameters and a larger, randomly selected line sample. The impact of these selections on the radial velocity measurements was assessed through a sample of 16 stellar activity-rich stars and measurements of their activity-induced signals. The results indicated that while both line samples produced stable signal distributions, there were noticeable differences in their precision and bias. These findings were interpreted using line sample properties and the characteristics of the lines that significantly influence activity-induced signals. Given that certain physical properties of lines are often unknown, especially in massive star spectra, the line samples' features were instead used to predict activity-induced signal distributions. The validity of this approach was confirmed by comparing the predictions with the actual measurements made of three solar-analog and one chemically peculiar star.

This research proposes a 2-phase WSN data collection method, starting with a 3D histogram-based link quality estimation to enhance the accuracy of link quality assessments. Next, the CPDA algorithm uses these estimates to create multiple disjoint route sets between nodes and the sink, ensuring a rapid, high-quality, and energy-efficient data transfer. Simulations indicate that CPDA outperforms existing methods like HRP and AOP in terms of average collection error, convergence speed, average route quality, and overall collection time.

This paper aims to present the contextual information associated with objects
identified by a deep-based object detector, by first examining the nature of
background context and then exploring the connection between an object and its
surrounding environment. To address this, a method is proposed that uses a
set of parallel convolutional networks to simultaneously detect objects and
contextual information and to learn the relationship between the two. This
approach employs a contextual descriptor network and a context-aware object
detector network. The proposed method is comprehensive and can be implemented
with different types of contextual information and detection methods. Experimental
results on the PASCAL VOC 2007 dataset demonstrate the method's effectiveness,
showing significant improvements in detection accuracy and context prediction.
The context predicted by the proposed context descriptor network is found to be
more relevant than that predicted by baseline models, including random guessing,
background prediction, and object patch embedding. Context is also shown to be
useful for the object detector, leading to significant performance gains when
utilized with both the proposed context and a specific type of context called
MC-context. The proposed context descriptor and the proposed descriptor's
features are found to be more descriptive of the scene context than the original
context and the descriptor's own features, respectively. A visual interface
is provided to show the context predicted by the proposed method, and a comparative
analysis with the original context and the context predicted by the baseline
models is provided.

The main objective of this paper is to investigate a system of Kirchhoff type elliptic equations that incorporates a set of growth restrictions and an exponential growth term. To analyze this problem, we utilize a ring-shaped domain and an admissible kernel function, and we establish both compactness and non-compactness cases for the embedding of Sobolev spaces. Additionally, the proof of compactness involves establishing uniform boundedness, compactness on sublevels, and compactness on sequence levels for the Kirchhoff map, and we employ a recent development in critical variational systems to prove the existence of a set of ground state solutions.

We examine the concentration behavior of conditional independent binary random variables that evolve over time and depend on higher previous states. Our primary result establishes that sums of such variables satisfy a deviation bound nearly as potent as that of conditionally independent and identically distributed variables. If independence between variables is assumed, we prove that the underlying probability distribution must possess a Pinsker constant no less than one-fifth of unity. These findings have implications for analyzing the concentration of gradient-based algorithms like stochastic and mini-batch methods.

Let $p$ be an odd prime and consider the ring of power series $R=W(\mathbb{F})[t]^{Sp}(p)$, where $W(\mathbb{F})$ is the ring of Witt vectors of a finite field $\mathbb{F}$ of characteristic $p$, and $Sp(p)$ denotes the ideal generated by $p$ and the polynomial $t^{p-1}$. For any finite-dimensional vector space $M$ over $\mathbb{F}$, we can construct a torsion $Sp(p)$-module $P(M)$ which serves as a classical relative Fontaine-Dieudonne theory to up-to-date schemes over $Sp(p)$. Additionally, we establish the functorial equivalence between the category of exact tensorial nilpotent $p$-adic SO-Deligne-Lusztig-bisets over $R$, denoted as $\mathcal{SH}(R)$, and the category of finite-dimensional vector spaces over $\mathbb{F}$.

Our calculation predicts a sign change in the created dihadron asymmetry, specifically cos(phi_R), during SIDIS experiments where the quark and proton spins are reversed. This prediction could help differentiate between twist-3 quark scalar and chiral odd gaudin toroidal moments during SIDIS experiments. Moreover, we found that the created dihadron cross-section and asymmetry are influenced by the interaction between quark scalar density and the proton intrinsic spin density, as well as interactions between chiral odd GMMs and a twist-2 target density. Notably, we also identified an interference between quark chiral odd GMMs and the quark twist-3 distribution moments that contributes to the created dihadron cross-section and asymmetry, specifically cos(phi_R). This interference could provide insight and constraints when studying 3-dimensional intrinsic spin density matrix distributions via dihadron production data analysis. Additionally, our interference term introduces a new source of T-odd correlation that needs to be considered when analyzing data from the PHENIX and STAR experiments to accurately interpret their measurements of T-odd dihadron asymmetries.

We've established recently, 2nd-order perturbation theory, applicable to long-standing cosmological binary systems, can be expanded to 3rd-order perturbation theory under specific conditions. We've now examined its performance in a de Sitter universe, a key component of $\Lambda$-dominated cosmology. Our tests reveal that, in a de Sitter universe, the 3rd-order perturbation can be incorporated into a comprehensive, perturbation-based model that accurately replicates the motion of binary systems, even as the universe expands. This reveals that, unlike other $\Lambda$-cosmology models, the de Sitter model doesn't necessitate new forces, but rather reflects the influence of cosmology on local systems. We propose that if our universe continues to expand, we may witness the emergence of a new 'de Sitter realm', a realm where the 3rd-order perturbation becomes a prominent feature of the universe.

Let $(V,\omega)$ and $(W,\mu)$ be symplectic spaces. A linear transformation $f$ from $V$ to $W$ is termed a symplectic converter when it transforms any subspace of $V$ that maintains the $\omega$-nondegeneracy property, into a corresponding $\mu$-nondegenerate subspace of $W$. If, furthermore, $f$ maps every $\omega$-nondegenerate subspace, into a $\mu$-nondegenerate subspace, it is called a strong symplectic converter. This paper aims to provide a symplectic analogue to a previously established result regarding positive-definite quadratic forms.

This paper presents a Wikipedia-based entity recommendation framework that utilizes an e-rank index to suggest entities on the Yahoo! Knowledge Graph (YKG). Unlike traditional ranking methods, e-rank employs a layered graph structure to model entity relationships, combining reachability and centrality metrics to determine entity importance. To address issues with reachability in directed graphs, we incorporated the concept of virtual nodes to create reachability strong components, thereby enhancing graph reachability and improving entity ranking results. Our approach effectively leverages entity relationship information to provide accurate recommendations and outperforms entity centrality-based methods on the YKG.

Accepting previously unmatched kidneys offers an opportunity to save more lives through transplantation, but it requires balancing the needs of these new donors with those of the original kidney donors and recipients.
